title: Inside America’s first new submarine base abroad for 53 years

vocab.articleQuote: giving Australia a more potent deterrent
vocab.meaning: A deterrent is something that makes people afraid to do a bad thing, so they decide not to. A big, loud guard dog is a deterrent to a burglar, and a strict teacher is a deterrent to passing notes. In the article, Australia's new submarines would be a deterrent: other countries would think twice before attacking.
examples: The bright porch light is a deterrent to people sneaking around our yard.
A big fine is a deterrent to dropping trash in the park.

vocab.articleQuote: particularly those who have always been sceptical of its alliance
vocab.meaning: Sceptical means not sure that something is true or a good idea, and wanting more proof first. If a friend says he can eat twenty tacos, you might be sceptical until you see it. In the article, some Australians are sceptical of their country's close alliance with America. (Americans usually spell it skeptical.)
examples: I was sceptical that the old bike could still go fast, so I tested it.
My mom was sceptical of my plan to clean my room in five minutes.

vocab.articleQuote: America and Britain have both had to revamp a slew of laws
vocab.meaning: To revamp something is to change it a lot so it is newer or works better. A team might revamp its practice plan after a losing season, and a family might revamp a messy garage into a play space. In the article, America and Britain had to revamp many laws so they could share secret technology.
examples: We revamped our club's website to make it easier to use.
The cafeteria was revamped over the summer with new tables and a new menu.

concepts.name: Alliance
concepts.articleQuote: the innermost sanctum of American alliances
concepts.meaning:
Why would one country let another country's navy live on its land? Because the two have an **alliance**: a formal agreement between countries to help and protect each other.

Think of a group of kids who promise, "If anyone bothers one of us, all of us stand up for them." Each kid is safer, and each one also owes something back.

Countries do the same thing, but with written promises. Allies share information, train together, and sometimes let each other use bases. The price is that an ally can get pulled into the other's problems, and some people at home may not like that.

In the article, Australia is a close ally of America, so American submarines will be based at Australia's Stirling base. Some Australians are sceptical of the deal because they worry it ties their country too closely to America.

So the takeaway: an alliance is a promise to help each other, and it brings both safety and obligations.

concepts.name: Nuclear power vs. nuclear weapons
concepts.articleQuote: no nuclear weapons are involved, only nuclear power
concepts.meaning:
Does a nuclear-powered submarine carry nuclear bombs? No. **Nuclear power** and **nuclear weapons** are two different things that both come from splitting atoms.

Think of fire. A campfire heats your hands and cooks your food, but a fire out of control burns the forest. Same basic fire, very different use.

In a nuclear power plant, the splitting is slow and controlled, and the heat it makes turns into energy. A submarine can use this to make electricity and push itself through the water for years without refuelling. A nuclear weapon is built to release all the energy at once in a giant explosion.

In the article, the submarines at Stirling run on nuclear power, so they can travel much farther than diesel boats without coming up to the surface. The article says no nuclear weapons are involved.

So the takeaway: nuclear power is controlled energy for running things, and it is not the same as a nuclear weapon.

quiz.question: Why did workers have to build seahorse hotels at the Stirling base?
options: Seahorses are bad swimmers, so they were moved to safe grids before the construction
The navy wanted to keep seahorses as pets
quiz.explanation: Seahorses hook onto rocks and piers, so divers moved 263 of them before the base was upgraded.

quiz.question: What is AUKUS?
options: A deal between America, Australia and Britain to design and build nuclear-powered submarines together
quiz.explanation: AUKUS was announced in 2021 by the three countries.

quiz.question: Why is Stirling a useful place for American submarines?
options: It is out of range of all but the most advanced Chinese missiles, yet closer to Asian waters than other American submarine bases
It has the biggest cricket field in the world
It is the only place with a pier
quiz.explanation: The article says this is its big advantage over existing bases, including the one at Guam.

quiz.question: What is the big worry about AUKUS?
options: Shipyards in America and Britain may not be able to build submarines fast enough
Nobody wants to be a sailor
quiz.explanation: American and British shipyards would need to build faster, or Australia could end up with a base but no submarines of its own.

quiz.question: How do the nuclear-powered subs help Australia, compared with its diesel-powered boats?
options: They can travel much farther without coming to the surface
quiz.explanation: Nuclear power lets subs range farther, which gives Australia a stronger deterrent.
